solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Page at front of work annals is complicated labour observation?

indicators.note: says the page letter stands before the rest
complicated letters are tangled up, so the words work annals is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader finds the yearly records of some piece of work hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges WORK ANNALS IS into ARKINSONSLAW. The question mark flags that 'labour observation' is a playful description: an observation about work.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous adage holds that work expands to fill the time available, a wry remark about labour.

clue.text: Office worker or newsagent?

definitions.meaning: a clerk who shuffles documents all day
playfully, someone who pushes papers across the counter, a seller of newspapers

explanation.surface: Is a person a clerk or the shopkeeper selling papers?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical literal reading, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucratic clerk is disparagingly called this, and a newsagent literally deals in newspapers.

clue.text: Cut short argument about describing historic writing

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, here the last of the quarrel word

parts.note: a run-in is a quarrel or argument
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly ends a debate about how old documents are described.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to runes, the ancient Germanic alphabet, so it describes historic script.

clue.text: Popular headgear for supporter, perhaps, is not entirely sensible

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fan is one example of a supporter
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A trendy hat for a football follower is a little silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headgear for supporter' means the supporter's own hat, so the supporter piece comes first; tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish behaviour lacks full adult good sense, so 'not entirely sensible' is a mild synonym.

clue.text: Coastal city having marine name I overlooked

parts.note: the marine realm is the sea

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so the letter I is dropped from the name word

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: A seaside town has a nautical name, but someone missed it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington city lies on Puget Sound on the Pacific coast of the USA.

clue.text: Noted Swede taking article from Middle East country, heading North

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading from bottom to top
taking the article away from the country removes those letters

parts.note: Lebanon is a country in the Middle East
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A famous Swede travels north out of a Middle Eastern country, removing some goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' removes the article, and 'heading North' reads what is left from the bottom of the down entry up, giving LEBON reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish inventor of dynamite, founded the prizes bearing his surname.

clue.text: Tall trees in line upon line — and two further

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits upon, above, the next

parts.note: a ley line is a supposed alignment, so ley can mean line
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Tall trees grow in row after row, with a couple more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: These fast-growing conifers are planted as hedges and become notoriously tall in British gardens.

clue.text: Get a reduced alcoholic drink

indicators.note: reduced means shortened, so the drink loses its last letter

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone orders a half-measure of booze.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to obtain or get it, as in winning a prize.

clue.text: Back cuts in political manipulation

indicators.note: back signals reading the word for cuts in the reverse direction

parts.note: nips are small cuts or snips

explanation.surface: A government supports spending cuts through media manipulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of news by political press officers to favour their party.

clue.text: Extravagant chap imprisoning youngster in apartment

indicators.note: in places that combined piece inside the apartment word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the man word encloses the boy word

parts.note: a chap is a man
a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A flashy fellow keeps a lad locked up in his flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, ostentatious and lavish behaviour can be called flamboyant or extravagant.

clue.text: District about to be encapsulated by policeman in Court

indicators.note: encapsulated by means enclosed inside, so the word for about goes within the policeman

parts.note: PC is a police constable
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An area is about to be summed up by an officer giving evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is a defined area of a town or a police district, especially in the USA.

clue.text: Story about area is work in collaboration

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fib word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a story can be a lie or fib

explanation.surface: A tale about a region turns out to be a group project.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and keep in contact with others, working together.

clue.text: Nothing in outrageous claims supported endlessly rising popular websites

indicators.note: in places the zero letter within the jumbled letters
outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of claims are rearranged

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, reversed
endlessly removes the last letter of the word for supported

parts.note: aided means supported or helped

explanation.surface: Wild claims of nothing, propped up, keep spreading across popular sites online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges the letters to SCIALM, with the zero placed inside; 'endlessly' leaves AIDE, which 'rising' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Facebook, Twitter and similar platforms are widely used websites for sharing content among users.

clue.text: Muscle revealed in group ignoring initial rigged prices

indicators.note: ignoring the initial means dropping the first letter of the group word

parts.note: a squad is a group, as of soldiers or players

indicators.note: rigged prices are fixed or tampered with, so the letters of prices are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muscle is exposed when a team overlooks the early sign of price-fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: The large four-part muscle at the front of the thigh extends the knee.

clue.text: One's charged expert to pen last article

indicators.note: to pen means to enclose, so the skilful word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
the end is the last part
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A specialist writes the final piece in a series.
explanation.definitionFit: In court the accused person facing a criminal accusation is the one charged.

clue.text: Emphasise snub about trophy

indicators.note: about means round, so the snub word goes round the trophy word

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
a pot is slang for a trophy or cup

explanation.surface: Someone stresses an insult concerning a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a stage light on something figuratively draws attention to it, highlighting it.

clue.text: Steer clear of love

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment in northern English speech, as in 'all right, love?'

explanation.surface: Keep well away from romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a friendly form of address in the English Midlands and North, like 'love' or 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducking means dodging, and the same word is a colloquial endearment used like dear.

clue.text: Recipe expert: he is beset by Celsius and Fahrenheit

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the word he goes between the two temperature letters

explanation.surface: A cook is troubled by oven settings in both temperature scales.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cook knows dishes and how to prepare them, an expert on recipes.

clue.text: English provoking humour about working without trying too hard

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the funny word goes round the working word

parts.note: comical means funny, provoking laughter
on means working or operating, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: An English comedian raises laughs about the job with minimal effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sparing with effort or resources means doing just enough, using little beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Avoiding the web? It's tripe, having no answer in English

indicators.note: having no means lacking, so the letter for answer is dropped

parts.note: tripe is offal, edible animal innards

explanation.surface: Someone shuns the internet, calling it rubbish with no answer in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like nonsense; it is the meat. OFFAL without A gives OFFL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disconnected from the internet means not using it, so one is keeping away from the net.

clue.text: Wife and daughter leaving soak — it's a hard decision

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the daughter letter drops out of the soak word

parts.note: to drench is to soak

explanation.surface: A wife and daughter walk out on a drunk, which is a painful choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' suggests a heavy drinker; here it is the verb drench.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful parting or tough emotional choice, such as leaving home, is called a wrench.

clue.text: Earlier race taking hour in open country

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary race before the final

explanation.surface: A preliminary race lasting an hour takes place in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncultivated land covered with heather and gorse is a type of open countryside.

clue.text: When game will end, without interruptions?

definitions.meaning: the final whistle point at which a match finishes
playfully, working every hour of the week, as in a permanent job

explanation.surface: A match goes on to its conclusion uninterrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is loose, hence the question mark: a full-time job takes up the whole working week.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the referee signals the finish of the match; full-time work fills the working week.

clue.text: Little space in core elements of oratorios for singer

indicators.note: in places the little space inside the central letters
the core of a word is its centre, here the middle three letters of oratorios

parts.note: an en is a small printing space, half an em

explanation.surface: A small gap appears in the heart of some choral works written for vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male voice and singer between baritone and alto.

clue.text: Increasing variety of cages to imprison Spaniard, say

indicators.note: imprison means enclose, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
a variety of a word is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: a Spaniard is one example of a Latin, a speaker of a Romance language

explanation.surface: More and more cage designs are being used to lock up a man from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' gives the rearrangement ESCAG, which is split to hold the Spaniard piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something escalating is rising or growing rapidly, like costs that keep going up.

clue.text: After upset, manages to forget work for an instant

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, reading upward
to forget the work means it is left out

parts.note: copes means manages
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: After a setback, someone manages to put their job out of mind for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forget' leaves CES, which 'upset' reads upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec is a casual shortening of second, a very brief moment, as in 'wait a sec'.

clue.text: Uncovered suggestion that should see golf banned

indicators.note: banned means excluded, so the golf letter is removed

parts.note: a nudge is a hint or suggestion
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hint is laid bare that golf should be outlawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked means being bare, without any clothes covering the body.

clue.text: A chance matter, relocating to this locality

indicators.note: relocating means moving around, so the letters of a chance matter are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Moving house to a neighbourhood is a matter of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain parents may move into a school's catchment area so their child qualifies for a place, which is the chance matter of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The district served by a school or hospital, from which it draws its users, is a locality.
